weeks.title: BFCM runs on pacing: the days before Friday decide it
weeks.dek: Northbeam and Triple Whale data both say the run-up carries the weekend: a third of BFCM revenue starts before the week, and Black Friday was the only day MER fell last year. Meta's conversion rate turned up in the latest index, and higher-AOV brands are winning 2026.

items.headline: Meta click-through rates are up more than 40% a year since January
items.take: Across all Meta placements in the 1,000+ accounts Northbeam tracks (about $6 billion of spend), average CTR has risen nonstop since January 2025, cooled around Prime Day 2026 and is climbing again. Bryan Bumgardner reads it as Meta optimising for clicks as the signal Apple can't hide.
items.why: Higher CTR alongside the falling conversion rates in Northbeam's weekly index means judge ads on what happens after the click, not on hook metrics.
items.label: Meta CTR
points: All placements (Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram), 1,000+ ad accounts, around $6B in ad spend
Average CTR rising since January 2025; cooled around Prime Day 2026, improving again
Bumgardner's hypotheses: Meta shifting toward engagement signals, and more click data feeding its models
items.quote: Clickthrough rates on Meta Ads are up more than 40% year-over-year since January.

items.headline: Howland's 58-point BFCM checklist: early access ads live by 10 November
items.take: Curtis Howland's free checklist runs from email authentication to ad approvals. His dates: early access ads on 10 November, sale ads on 14 November, every ad approved by 20 November with backups, a site code freeze from 19 November to 2 December and nothing new launched from 26 to 30 November.
items.why: If early access isn't live by tomorrow, you're behind his calendar; turn off Meta rules that pause ads on high CPA before the sale.
items.label: BFCM checklist
points: Launch early access Nov 10 and sale ads Nov 14
Get every ad approved by Nov 20, plus backups
Freeze site code and apps from Nov 19 to Dec 2; launch nothing new Nov 26 to 30
Keep the spam rate under 0.1%; one send a day and two on Nov 30
Check new-customer CPA before you cut an ad
items.quote: Launch early access Nov 10 and sale ads Nov 14.

items.headline: Pilothouse: Meta should record at least 90% of your Shopify orders
items.take: Pilothouse's pre-BFCM tracking check compares deduplicated Purchase events in Events Manager with Shopify online-store orders over the last 7, 14 and 28 days, and aims for at least 90% capture. The same issue warns Meta may add offers it detects on your site to duplicated ads.
items.why: Run the match-rate check this week, before 12 Nov and before budgets go up, and switch off Detected offers in Commerce Manager if you don't want Meta adding discounts to copied ads.

items.headline: Three Meta attribution tests to run, or park, before BFCM
items.take: Pilothouse's sequence: 7-day click + 1-day view against 7-day click only, then a 1-day click window, then incremental attribution in a separate campaign, all compared on 7-day click ROAS. Tests that straddle 12 Nov may move because of on-device measurement, not the setting.
items.why: If you can't finish a clean test before 12 Nov with enough purchases, keep the current setting through the sale.
items.quote: If your test runs across that date, results might shift

items.label: Ad costs
items.headline: Midterms lifted Meta CPMs about 10% everywhere, and prices haven't come back down
items.take: Across Haus brands, Meta CPMs in a typical market were up about 10% year on year from 1 Oct to Election Day, not just in contested races: NYC +9%, LA +8%, Detroit +12%, Anchorage +19%. Conversion rates didn't rise to compensate, so pixel-attributed efficiency was about 8% worse than August. Google CPCs rose about 4% and YouTube CPMs 6%.
items.why: Don't plan BFCM off an October baseline as if it were normal: you're starting from costs about a tenth higher, and last year BFCM week added over 50% on top. Set break-even CPA and ROAS floors now and judge the week on blended numbers.
items.src: Haus (Tyler Horner, posted by Olivia Kory) on X, 10 Nov 2026
items.quote: Meta CPMs rose across all markets, not just contested ones.

chart.title: Meta CPM change year on year, 1 Oct to Election Day 2026 (Haus brands)

points: The rise came early: about +10% in September against +6% in the last week of October; 2024 was the reverse, flat in September then +14% late in October
About two thirds of Haus brands saw pixel-attributed efficiency fall against August
Google CPCs up about 4%, YouTube CPMs up 6%
Prices hadn't normalised going into the BFCM run-up; in BFCM week 2025 CPMs rose over 50%

items.label: Offer design
items.headline: One-hour flash sales tripled Hollow's hourly revenue on Black Friday
items.take: In Foxwell's BFCM playbook with Brad Ploch, Hollow ran one-hour flash sales with a free beanie on orders over $100, which tripled hourly revenue and lifted AOV 30%. Moving from buy three get three free to buy two get two free cut CAC faster than it cut AOV, so margin per customer rose.
items.why: Give the week a few timed moments rather than one flat discount: a short flash window with a gift threshold above your AOV, BFCM-specific creative, and budget weighted to Black Friday morning and Cyber Monday evening.
items.quote: Yes, 3x your normal hourly revenue.

stat.label: Hollow's hourly revenue during one-hour Black Friday flash sales
stat.sub: Free beanie on orders over $100; AOV up 30%.

points: BFCM-specific creative beat evergreen ads last year
Black Friday mornings and Cyber Monday evenings carry the revenue; the weekend slump in between is normal
Smaller bundle (buy two get two) cut CAC faster than AOV, raising margin per customer

items.label: Measurement
items.headline: Northbeam: a weak incrementality test is worse than none, and BFCM is the easiest way to ruin one
items.take: Northbeam lists four ways a geo holdout test fails: it's too small to detect a real effect, the test regions don't look like the rest of your market, something changes mid-test (a spend shift, a big promotion, a new campaign without the holdout exclusion), or it ends before the channel's sales have landed. Meta converts within a few weeks; CTV and upper-funnel sales can take two months.
items.why: Don't start a geo holdout that runs into BFCM: the promotions and budget swings are exactly the mid-test changes that pollute it. Plan tests for January, size them before launch, and set the length from your conversion lag, not a default two weeks.
items.quote: A weak test can be worse than no test, because it gives you false confidence.

stat.label: of budget a platform may try to push into the 80% of geos left on in a 20% holdout
stat.sub: Northbeam: cap spend in treatment geos at normal levels, or the comparison is distorted.

points: Underpowered: run a power calculation and set a minimum detectable effect before launch
Biased: test and control geos must behave like the wider market
Polluted: spend shifts, big promotions, platform tactic changes or setup errors mid-test invalidate it; check daily that spend isn't leaking into holdout geos
Too short: if most sales from a dollar arrive 30 days later, a two-week test undercounts
Re-check any design more than seven days old on fresh data before launch

items.headline: ChatGPT opens a business dashboard showing how often it mentions your brand
items.take: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta on 10 Nov: verified businesses can update their details and product feed, and once past OpenAI's reporting thresholds see how often ChatGPT mentions them, click-throughs and the topics they're found through. The same issue notes TikTok Shop Plus, a $9.99-a-month pilot for 1M+ top US shoppers, with member deals through TikTok's 11 to 30 Nov BFCM event.
items.why: Claim and verify the ChatGPT profile and product feed before BFCM, then check AI referrals against orders in your own analytics. If you sell on TikTok Shop, check which products carry a Plus badge before briefing creators.
items.quote: see how often ChatGPT mentions you in its regular answers

items.headline: Black Friday was the only BFCM day MER fell last year: don't overspend into Friday
items.take: Across Northbeam's DTC customers, Black Friday 2025 took the biggest spend increase (+13.5% YoY) and was the only day MER fell (-2.8%). A third of BFCM revenue came from touchpoints before the week even started. Meanwhile the index for w/e 8 Nov shows Meta conversion rate back up 3.09% and ROAS up 3.35%.
items.why: Set hourly revenue targets from last year's curve, scale on accrual (click-date) numbers, and hold the Friday budget back rather than chasing a midday spike.
items.label: BFCM pacing
items.quote: Don't overspend into Friday, friends.

stat.label: Black Friday 2025 MER YoY, the only BFCM day that fell
stat.sub: Northbeam DTC customers, excluding Amazon; spend +13.5% that day.

points: 33% of BFCM 2025 revenue (42% of Black Friday's) came from touchpoints before the week
Scale on accrual (click-date) numbers, check business health on cash
Pace by the hour against last year's curve: Black Friday runs early, Cyber Monday peaks 7 to 8pm PT
Ridge moved AppLovin from a planned 5% to 10% of spend to 40% when Meta lagged in BFCM 2024

items.headline: Meta's conversion rate turns up and its share climbs past 56%
items.take: In the week ending 8 Nov, Meta CVR rose 3.09% and ROAS 3.35% with CPM flat (-0.56%) and new-customer CAC down 3.02%. Meta's budget share rose to 56.21%. TikTok got pricier (CPM +8.09%, CTR -11.64%), while Snapchat CVR jumped 17.74%.
items.why: The first weekly CVR gain after three straight falls: a good week to lock BFCM baselines, but one week is not a trend.

items.headline: Higher-AOV brands are winning 2026: $500+ AOV median revenue up 31%
items.take: Northbeam's Q3 2026 benchmarks by AOV band show the median $500+ brand grew revenue 31.1% and new-customer revenue 31.9% on 21.8% more spend. At $50-$100 AOV, median revenue fell 6.8%. New-customer CAC rose at the median in every band except $200-$500.
items.why: If your AOV is under $100, bundles and thresholds that lift basket size may do more for BFCM efficiency than another bid change.

$50-$100 AOV median: revenue -6.8%, new-customer MER -7.3%

items.quote: High AOV brands are outperforming this year.

items.headline: The four days before Black Friday did 61% of the weekend's revenue at nearly the same return
items.take: Howland, in a Triple Whale partner post, uses Triple Whale's 2025 data: $1.77B revenue on $396.6M spend (4.5x) for 24-27 Nov against $2.88B on $606.6M (4.7x) over the weekend. His brands put the offer live around 15 Nov in its own campaign, test for a week, then scale from 23 Nov.
items.why: Plan the scale-up for 23 Nov, not Friday, and keep the sale in a separate campaign you can switch off on 1 Dec.
items.label: BFCM ramp
points: 24-27 Nov 2025: $1.77B revenue on $396.6M ad spend, 4.5x
Ramp: offer live by 15 Nov in its own campaign, test to 22 Nov, scale from 23 Nov, offer off 1 Dec

stat.label: of BFCM weekend revenue made in the four days before, at 4.5x vs 4.7x
stat.sub: Triple Whale BFCM 2025 data, via Curtis Howland (paid partnership post).

items.headline: Match every step of the BFCM ad on the landing page, from hook to discount code
items.take: Howland lays out eight questions a shopper asks (hook, event, offer, hero, math, proof, clock, close) and pairs each ad answer with the same answer on the lander: one offer number above the fold, savings in dollars, an end date with a timer, the code at the top.
items.why: Check each BFCM ad against its lander: the same callout, sale name and offer number should appear in both.

Offer and math: one number, then the saving in dollars
Clock and close: name the end day, run a timer, put the code at the top

weeks.title: Meta's prices pause, its conversions don't
weeks.dek: Northbeam publishes the most detailed Black Friday rulebook of the season while its own index shows Meta conversion rate falling for a third straight week. Meanwhile, Meta and Google both change what gets measured, three weeks before the sale.

items.headline: Black Friday ads that led with proof ran 16 days at the median, not 10
items.take: Howland sorted his 68,245 Black Friday 2025 Meta ads into ten looks. Price-led ads were 12% of brands' ads and proof-led 17%, almost all creator video at 15%. Brands that made proof ads ran all their ads longer: a 16-day median against 10 for all ads.
items.why: Don't ship only discount tiles: pair a big-number ad with a creator or comparison ad, and have early access live by 10 Nov and sale ads by 14 Nov.

items.headline: Northbeam's Black Friday rulebook: four check-ins a day, 20% bumps, reset every night
items.take: Bryan Bumgardner's survival guide turns Northbeam's client playbook into rules you can set up now. Cap every budget raise at 20%, review four times a day from 25 Nov to 1 Dec, and use a 12:01am rule to reopen each campaign at 30% above the previous day's start.
figs: CPMs +20% to 35% over last year's big weekend
items.why: It's the most specific BFCM operating plan any source has published this year. Our deep dive breaks down all eight rules and where we'd bend them.
items.label: The Black Friday rulebook
items.src: Northbeam, The Media Buyer, 5 Nov 2026, worked example in the guide
points: Week of 10/25-11/01: Meta CPM -0.11%, CTR +4.86%, CPC -4.87%, new-customer CAC +1.50%, CVR -5.05%, ROAS +1.54%; budget share 55.25% (-0.74)
Google share 18.00% (+0.74), CPM +3.95%; TikTok CAC -9.24%, CVR +12.95%; Snapchat CVR -21.44%; Pinterest CAC +11.97%
Last November Meta-side CPMs spiked 20% to 35% over the big weekend, stalling cost-cap and bid-cap campaigns
Playbook: four check-ins a day, budget bumps of 20% at most, a 12:01 am rule resetting budgets to 30% above the prior day's start

items.headline: Meta conversion rate falls for a third straight week as CPMs go flat
items.take: In Northbeam's Media Buyer Index for the week ending 1 Nov, Meta CPM barely moved (-0.11%) and CPC fell 4.87%, but CVR dropped 5.05%. That follows falls of 1.63% and 2.88% in the two weeks before. Google's budget share rose to 18.00% (+0.74 pts) as Meta's slipped to 55.25%.
items.why: Cheaper clicks aren't turning into orders. Conversion, not cost, is the number to defend going into the sale.

items.headline: Howland's BFCM budget curve: 150 to 200% on Black Friday and Cyber Monday
items.take: Answering questions from 8 to 9 figure DTC brands, Curtis Howland lays out a daily budget shape, as a share of BFCM daily budget: 100% Monday to Wednesday, 120% Thanksgiving, 150 to 200% Black Friday, 130% over the weekend, 150 to 200% Cyber Monday, then 80% the Tuesday after. Last year Black Friday day-one CPMs in his accounts ran 45% above the week before.
figs: BF day-1 CPMs +45% vs prior week
items.why: Read it alongside Northbeam's rules. Howland sets each day's budget; Northbeam's check-ins steer spend within the day.

features.title: Northbeam's hour-by-hour BFCM playbook, taken apart
features.dek: Northbeam's founders on the Marketing Operators podcast, summarised by Bryan Bumgardner: the weekend is won in the weeks before it, Black Friday ROAS flatters you, and the best operators pace by the hour. What it says, what it means, and where we'd push back.
features.byline: Newsroom analysis of The Media Buyer, 12 Nov 2026 (Northbeam), read with the same issue's index for w/e 8 Nov and this week's other BFCM sources.
headlines: Pace Q4 like a marathon, not one day

Upper funnel (TV, YouTube, streaming, partnerships) works through early November; from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday the budget shifts to Meta, AppLovin and Google Search to catch the intent you built.
Launch BFCM ads early

Ridge's Black Friday ads go live early in November, so by Thanksgiving week the ads carrying the budget have run 12 to 14 days. That made scaling from $100k to $400k a day realistic. Northbeam warns against counting on brand-new ads to scale that week.
The run-up earns the weekend
In BFCM 2025 the median Northbeam customer got 33% of BFCM revenue from touchpoints before the week started, 42% for Black Friday alone, with 4.1 touchpoints before buying.
Black Friday ROAS flatters you

In-platform Meta reporting credits the sale to the day it happens (cash basis), so Friday collects credit for earlier ads and looks great. Northbeam's rule: scale on accrual (credit to the click date), check business health on cash.
Pace by the hour

Ridge tracks revenue hourly against last year's curve plus its growth target. If 40% of the day's revenue landed by noon last year and today's forecast is $150,000, you should be at $60,000 by noon. The curve differs by day: Thanksgiving runs late, Black Friday early, Cyber Monday peaks around 7 to 8pm PT.
Black Friday is where efficiency breaks

Across Northbeam DTC customers (excluding Amazon), Black Friday 2025 took the biggest YoY spend increase, 13.5%, and was the only day MER fell, by 2.8%. Saturday and Sunday took the smallest increases and gained the most efficiency.
Move budget when the data says so
In BFCM 2024 Meta underperformed for Ridge; AppLovin drove a similar share of new visits at better ROAS, so Ridge took it from a planned 5% to 10% of spend to 40%, about $200,000 a day.
Keep paid on new customers
Before BFCM keep new visits high; during the sale email and SMS reach existing customers, so point paid media at net-new buyers.
analysis: The issue's numbers and Howland's Triple Whale numbers this week point the same way from two datasets. Northbeam: a third of BFCM revenue comes from touchpoints before the week, and Black Friday is the one day efficiency falls. Triple Whale (via Howland): the four days before Black Friday did 61% of the weekend's revenue at 4.5x against 4.7x. Both say the run-up is under-funded relative to Friday.

The accrual point matters more than it looks. If a third of the revenue that lands on Friday was earned by earlier clicks, in-platform Friday ROAS is inflated by exactly the spend that was cut earlier in the week. Teams that scale on Friday's cash-basis ROAS end up paying the most on the least efficient day, which is what the 13.5% spend and -2.8% MER show.

The same issue's index (w/e 8 Nov) gives some room: Meta's conversion rate rose 3.09% and ROAS 3.35% with CPM flat, the first weekly CVR gain after three straight falls, while Haus put midterm-season CPMs about 10% higher across the board. Prices are high, but the click-to-order rate is no longer sliding, at least for one week.

The Ridge examples are large-account stories (up to $400k a day, $200k a day on AppLovin). The principle, holding a plan but moving budget when a channel's new-visit share and ROAS say so, works at any size; the 40% AppLovin move needs a measurement setup most brands don't have.
actions: By 14 Nov
Pull last year's hourly revenue curve for Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Cyber Monday, and set this year's hourly targets from it plus your growth target.
By 15 Nov
Have BFCM ads live so the ones carrying budget have 12 to 14 days of data by Thanksgiving week.
By 18 Nov
Set your profitable one-day accrual ROAS by channel and agree who checks it, when.
23 to 26 Nov
Fund the four days before Black Friday; don't save the budget for Friday.
28 Nov
Cap Friday increases: scale only when accrual ROAS beats target, not on in-platform ROAS.
29 Nov to 1 Dec
Lean into Saturday and Sunday, where last year's efficiency held best; watch Cyber Monday's 7 to 8pm PT peak.
pushback: Click-date accounting is what Northbeam sells. Without an MTA tool, a workable stand-in is blended MER by day plus Meta's 7-day-click view, read the morning after.
Last year's curve is a guide, not a law: a different offer, launch time or email schedule moves the curve. Use it to catch drift, not to force spend.
The -2.8% is the median across Northbeam's base for one day. Brands with strong Black Friday-only offers may still want Friday spend; check your own 2025 hourly data first.
checklist: Profitable one-day accrual ROAS set per channel
Hourly revenue targets for each BFCM day
Budget planned for 23 to 26 Nov, not just Friday
Paid prospecting aimed at new customers during the sale

features.title: Northbeam's Black Friday playbook, taken apart
features.dek: Bryan Bumgardner's survival guide boils Northbeam's client work down to one discipline: check more often, bump in small steps, and reset every night. Here's what it says, what it's really telling you, what to do about it, and where we'd push back.
features.byline: Newsroom analysis of Northbeam's Black Friday Survival Guide: 2026 Edition (The Media Buyer, 5 Nov 2026), read with the same week's index and this week's other BFCM sources.
quote: Last November we saw CPMs spike 20% to 35% during the big weekend.
headlines: Check in four times a day, not two or three

Normally an account under $100k a day gets checked two or three times. For BFCM Northbeam wants a 9am read against the trailing seven days, a 2pm round of calls, a 7pm push and a final pass before bed. A slow morning isn't a verdict: a campaign under target for six to eight hours but on target over seven days gets left until the next check-in.
Never raise a budget more than 20% at a time

Northbeam's 'spend S-curve': on Meta, a budget change makes spend spike straight away and then taper off. Several small raises give steadier hourly delivery and spread the risk through the day. Northbeam calls the method 'scale and surf'.
Reset every budget at 12:01am

A rule reopens each campaign at 30% above the previous day's opening budget, not wherever it finished the night. In Northbeam's example, a campaign that opened at $10,000 and reached $20,000 by evening reopens the next day at $13,000. It guards against runaway spend, and mornings are quieter anyway while email and SMS land.
Expect cost caps and bid caps to stall

CPMs spiked 20% to 35% over last year's big weekend, and Bumgardner thinks this will be the most expensive BFCM yet. When a capped campaign can't spend, copy it into a lowest-cost twin. When one cap campaign's CPMs run away, move it to lowest cost with broader targeting.
Leave evergreen cost caps alone

Put the extra sale spend in separate max-conversion campaigns and switch those off when the sale ends. One Northbeam client cut its product-level cost caps after the weekend and had to rebuild performance from scratch.
Judge today's spend on today's results

During BFCM, measure spend on an accrual basis. Build one view per platform with blended revenue and blended cost per order by campaign, ad set and ad, showing today against the trailing three to seven days. Keep cash numbers for overall business health. It only works if your conversion-lag multipliers are already set.
Drop 'up to 50% off'

Pick one discount number, say it plainly in the caption, and put the call to action in the video. Northbeam says 'up to' is hurting click-through and reads like a credit-card mailer. BFCM creative captures demand you built during the year; it doesn't create it.
Audit Meta's Product Browsing AI enhancement
This ad-level setting can turn statics and video into product ads, which tends to pull prospecting toward retargeting. Turn it on or off on purpose, on every prospecting ad.
analysis: The guide is about tempo more than tactics. The 20% step is the same one Northbeam recommends all year. What changes is how often you take it (up to three times a day) and the nightly reset. Put together, the rules set a ceiling. Three 20% raises compound to about 1.73 times the morning budget by bedtime (our arithmetic). The 12:01 rule then pulls the next morning back to 1.3 times the previous opening budget. Left on autopilot, no campaign's opening budget grows faster than 30% a day.

Read it next to the numbers in the same issue. In the week ending 1 Nov, Meta CPM was flat (-0.11%) but conversion rate fell 5.05%, its third straight weekly decline, and Bumgardner says Meta conversion rates are at record lows. That's why the guide builds its cockpit on blended revenue and new-customer cost per order rather than in-platform ROAS. When clicks get cheaper but convert worse, platform ROAS can hold up while the business pays more for each customer.

The cost-cap warning has independent support. Curtis Howland says Black Friday day-one CPMs ran 45% above the week before in his accounts last year. Northbeam's weekly Meta CPM chart already runs about 24% above last year. A cap set on October costs is likely to stall over the weekend, which is exactly the case the lowest-cost twin is there for.

One thing the guide doesn't mention: Meta switches on on-device conversion measurement for every account on 12 Nov. Common Thread, citing Meta, says it adds up to 15% more attributed purchases. So in-platform numbers this BFCM won't compare cleanly with last year's, and a blended cockpit is the only stable yardstick.

The creative advice matches the data. Howland's study of 68,245 Black Friday ads found 50% was the median discount, 66.2% of ads led with percent off, and 64% of brands kept the same number into Black Friday week. Northbeam's 'pick one number and say it plainly' is what most brands already do. Removing 'up to' is the cheap win.
actions: By 11 Nov
Take a blended baseline before Meta's on-device measurement changes the numbers: Shopify revenue over total spend, and new-customer CAC, for the trailing 7, 14 and 28 days.
By 18 Nov
Build the cockpit: blended revenue and cost per order by campaign, ad set and ad, today against the trailing 7 days. Agree the conversion-lag multipliers you'll apply at the 9am read.
By 18 Nov
Split your structure. Evergreen cost caps stay untouched until December; the sale budget goes into separate max-conversion campaigns you can switch off on 2 Dec.
By 20 Nov
For every cap campaign you rely on, build a lowest-cost twin and leave it paused, ready to launch the moment the cap stalls.
By 20 Nov
Write the 12:01am reset rule (+30% on the prior day's opening budget) in Meta's automated rules and trial it on a low-stakes campaign first.
By 20 Nov
Audit Product Browsing and Advantage+ Creative enhancements on every prospecting ad, and record what's on and why.
Creative
Use one discount number, written in the caption, with no 'up to'. Get it live before the median brand's launch, 13 days out.
25 Nov to 1 Dec

Staff the 9am, 2pm, 7pm and late check-ins with a shared handoff doc. Set each day's budget from Howland's curve (Thanksgiving 120%, Black Friday 150 to 200%, weekend 130%, Cyber Monday 150 to 200%), then use Northbeam's 20% steps to steer within the day.
pushback: The 30% reset can starve a breakout day

Howland's accounts run Black Friday and Cyber Monday at 150 to 200% of daily budget. A strict 30% overnight cap won't get you there from Thanksgiving's open. Plan to override the reset on those two mornings rather than let the rule set your ceiling.
If you're running accounts on your own, automate the steps instead of skipping them: rules for the 20% raises on hitting target and for the 12:01 reset. Keep your own reviews for 9am and 7pm.
The S-curve is asserted, not shown
Northbeam bases it on a decade of observation but publishes no chart. Treat it as strong practitioner experience, and check your own hourly spend after a budget change this week.
'Most expensive BFCM ever' is a forecast
It's Bumgardner's opinion. Right now the index shows Meta CPM flat week to week, and the gap that matters is year on year (about +24%). Plan for the spike; don't assume it.
Accrual reads need lag you trust

Without conversion-lag multipliers, every 9am read will look worse than it really is, and the 'don't panic' rule does all the work. If you don't have multipliers yet, take them from last year's BFCM conversion timing this week.
checklist: Dashboard: blended revenue, new-customer revenue and CAC per campaign, today against trailing 7 days
12:01am budget reset rules written and tested
Four check-ins a day booked from 25 Nov to 1 Dec, with a handoff doc
Evergreen ads and cost caps left on and untouched
Lowest-cost twins ready for every cap campaign
Auto-DPA and Product Browsing setting checked on every prospecting ad
